title: Closures of points and irreducible closed subsets of the spectrum of a ring
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] its set of prime ideals with the Zariski topology, whose closed sets are the sets $V(I)=\{\mathfrak p\in X: I\subseteq\mathfrak p\}$ for ideals $I\subseteq R$. Then: (1) for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ the closure of the one-point set $\{\mathfrak p\}$ in $X$ is $V(\mathfrak p)$; in particular, for primes $\mathfrak p,\mathfrak p'$ one has $\mathfrak p'\in V(\mathfrak p)$ iff $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak p'$, and $V(\mathfrak p)\subseteq V(\mathfrak p')$ iff $\mathfrak p'\subseteq\mathfrak p$; (2) a subset $Z\subseteq X$ is closed and irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] if and only if $Z=V(\mathfrak p)$ for some prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$, and this prime is unique.
